guide.summary: Own app, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none); Public launch, Restricted Mode removed (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Own app, up to 25 outside users (self-serve (no review step found in the docs), wait none). Hardest: Public launch, Restricted Mode removed (app review, wait 2-4 weeks).

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth2 app for YNAB. Managed apps show Composio's name on the consent screen and share quota across Composio users.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes, since Composio provides a managed YNAB app. For a production launch you want your own app to get your branding, a dedicated quota, and a review that covers your own users.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio's
Dedicated rate limit quota rather than shared quota
Restricted Mode removal is requested for your own OAuth app
Managed apps use Composio's default scopes

scenarios.label: Own app, up to 25 outside users
scenarios.when_this_applies: Pilot or early access with 25 or fewer users other than the app owner, no review requested yet.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: No review is needed while staying within the Restricted Mode cap (c1).

scenarios.approval: No review while in Restricted Mode; the app is capped at 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.
extras: Restricted Mode: 25 access tokens for non-owner users.

modifiers.note: Restricted Mode: 25 access tokens for non-owner users.

scenarios.label: Public launch, Restricted Mode removed
scenarios.when_this_applies: Production agent product serving more than 25 YNAB users.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; privacy policy drafting included

scenarios.approval: YNAB reviews the app against its API Terms and OAuth Application Requirements before removing Restricted Mode.
extras: Capped at 25 non-owner tokens until review passes.
No copying YNAB products; naming and branding rules

modifiers.note: Capped at 25 non-owner tokens until review passes.
No copying YNAB products; naming and branding rules apply.

prerequisites.title: YNAB account with Developer Settings
prerequisites.detail: The OAuth app is created in the web app under Account Settings, then Developer Settings. No plan or program requirement was found.

prerequisites.title: Privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Publish a policy covering data handling, storage, security, retention, a deletion method and a Last Updated date. Show its URL in the OAuth client configuration and in your app.

prerequisites.title: Active YNAB subscription for each user
prerequisites.detail: API calls return 403 errors when the user's subscription has lapsed or trial has expired.

steps.title: Create OAuth app in YNAB
steps.detail: Sign in, open Account Settings then Developer Settings, click New Application, enter details and save. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.done_when: Client ID and Client Secret are visible.

steps.title: Copy Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and enter it in the YNAB app settings. It must match the one used in authorization requests.
steps.done_when: Redirect URI is saved in the YNAB app.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret. Request read-only scope unless writes are needed.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists for the ynab toolkit.

steps.title: Draft privacy policy and review answers
steps.detail: Draft a policy that meets YNAB's listed requirements and check the app name for the 'for YNAB' rule and the non-affiliation footer.
steps.done_when: Draft is ready for your review.

steps.title: Publish policy and submit review form
steps.detail: Publish the policy, add its URL to the OAuth client configuration, and submit the Restricted Mode review form.

steps.title: Wait for YNAB review
steps.detail: YNAB reviews the app and emails confirmation when Restricted Mode is removed.

traps.title: Access tokens have a general limit of 200 requests
traps.detail: Access tokens have a general limit of 200 requests per hour, on a rolling window.

traps.title: 25-user cap blocks new sign-ups silently to you
traps.detail: Once 25 tokens are issued, new users see a message on the authorization screen and cannot connect. Request review before you approach the cap.

traps.title: Review takes 2-4 weeks
traps.detail: Plan the launch date after submitting the review request, not before.

traps.title: Tokens expire after 2 hours
traps.detail: Implicit grant tokens cannot be refreshed, so users must re-authorize. Authorization code grant supports refresh tokens.

traps.title: Naming rules
traps.detail: The app name and its web address cannot include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by 'for'. Add a non-affiliation disclaimer in your site footer.

traps.title: Rate limit of 200 requests per hour per token
traps.detail: YNAB can change limits at its discretion, so build in backoff.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see Composio's name on the consent screen and share quota with other Composio users.

blockers.symptom: Authorization screen shows a limit message and refuses new users
blockers.what_it_means: The app reached 25 tokens in Restricted Mode.
blockers.what_to_do: Submit the review request form and wait for approval.
blockers.agent_can_help: Prepare the privacy policy draft and a compliance checklist.

blockers.what_it_means: The token was issued with read-only scope.
blockers.what_to_do: Re-authorize the user without the read-only scope.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the auth config scope settings.

open_questions: Does the review check anything beyond policy compliance and the privacy policy, such as a demo? Ask YNAB API support or the review form.
Does Composio's managed app count against its own 25-token cap? Ask Composio support.
Can Composio's callback be used as the redirect URI directly? Confirm in the Composio dashboard.

sources.title: YNAB integration launched! - #19 by shanaqui - Akrasia - Beeminder Forum

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Make sure to be logged into your YNAB account, go to your YNAB Developer Settings and create a new OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: A developer creates the YNAB OAuth application in YNAB Developer Settings while logged into their YNAB account. The page names no plan, region, or developer program requirement.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: If you would like to use this App, please authorize with YNAB!
evidence.answer: The page says end users authorize the app with YNAB. It does not mention any admin approval, allowlisting, or installation step.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Enter the URL of this project as a Redirect URI (in addition to the existing three options), then "Save Application."
evidence.answer: The project's URL is entered as a Redirect URI in the OAuth application settings, in addition to three existing options.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Copy your Client ID and Redirect URI into the src/config.json file of your project.
evidence.answer: After creating the OAuth application, the developer copies the Client ID and Redirect URI into the project's src/config.json file.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: | [YNAB](/toolkits/ynab.md) | `YNAB` |
evidence.answer: This page lists YNAB under the Composio-managed OAuth available section, meaning Composio supplies the OAuth app for YNAB.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so the developer does not need to register an OAuth app or supply a client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: A toolkit appears under **Composio-managed OAuth available** when Composio manages at least one OAuth method. Open the toolkit page to check each method.
evidence.answer: A toolkit appears under the Composio-managed OAuth section when Composio manages at least one OAuth method, and each method should be checked on the toolkit page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method, so YNAB's managed status should be checked per method on its toolkit page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Composio provides the OAuth app when the toolkit's composio_managed_auth_schemes field contains the OAuth method; otherwise the developer must register their own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scope: use the minimum viable scope. Prefer read-only unless the hosted connector explicitly offers write tools.
evidence.answer: The page advises using the minimum viable YNAB scope and preferring read-only unless the connector explicitly offers write tools.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: or workspace-admin approval before they expose or invoke custom-connector write tools, independent of the YNAB grant.
evidence.answer: For MCP clients (not YNAB itself), some clients may require developer/beta mode or workspace-admin approval before they expose or invoke custom-connector write tools, independent of the YNAB grant.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Create and verify a YNAB OAuth application with the production redirect URI.
evidence.answer: The YNAB OAuth application must be created and verified with the production redirect URI.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Public connector origin used to build the exact callback URI.
evidence.answer: The exact callback URI is built from the public connector origin configured as CONNECTOR_BASE_URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Authorization URL: https://app.ynab.com/oauth/authorize
evidence.answer: The YNAB authorization endpoint is on https://app.ynab.com and the token endpoint is on the same host.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: YNAB OAuth application client ID (Worker secret).
evidence.answer: The Worker needs the YNAB OAuth application's client ID, stored as a Worker secret.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: YNAB OAuth application secret (Worker secret).
evidence.answer: The Worker needs the YNAB OAuth application's client secret, stored as a Worker secret.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Configure the OAuth app with a privacy policy URL and display that URL clearly in the connector interface.
evidence.answer: The OAuth app should be configured with a privacy policy URL, which the connector interface should display clearly.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: PKCE: S256 code challenge and verifier
evidence.answer: The YNAB OAuth flow uses response type code and PKCE with S256 code challenge and verifier.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Use public names and DNS names that follow the "for YNAB" pattern and do not imply sponsorship, endorsement, or official YNAB support.
evidence.answer: Public names and DNS names should follow the 'for YNAB' pattern and must not imply sponsorship, endorsement, or official YNAB support.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Add non-affiliation language; this connector is not an official YNAB product.
evidence.answer: The connector should include non-affiliation language stating it is not an official YNAB product.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: In your OAuth app's settings, you set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint, using the example https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect (this applies when proxying the callback through your own domain).

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The example redirect URI on your own domain is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint on your domain receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio's callback URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio. The user's browser needs to be redirected so the OAuth flow completes correctly.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect; it must not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio, because the user's browser must be redirected.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: composio_url = "https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback"
evidence.answer: The page's example Composio callback target that the proxy redirects to is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token. Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: During OAuth the browser briefly redirects through backend.composio.dev so Composio can capture the auth token, and some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: To hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: This page is generic and does not mention YNAB; the consent screen shows Composio branding ("Composio wants to access your account") on providers such as Google and GitHub, and the stated fix is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own OAuth app
evidence.answer: The stated fix for the Composio-branded OAuth consent screen is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Adding your own OAuth app is recommended only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: `backend.composio.dev` flashes during OAuth redirect-back
evidence.answer: Users may briefly see backend.composio.dev in the browser address bar during OAuth redirect-back, and the stated fix is to proxy the redirect through your domain.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add a redirect proxy only when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.
evidence.answer: Add a redirect proxy only when the browser must stay on your domain during the OAuth callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **[Composio managed apps](/toolkits/managed-auth)**: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps (managed apps) for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so the developer does not register one. This is stated generally, not for YNAB; the page does not say whether YNAB has a managed app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **Custom auth configs**: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: With a custom auth config, the developer supplies their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see Composio's name on the OAuth consent screen rather than the developer's app name.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You're hitting rate limits.** Managed apps share quota across all Composio users. Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their API quota across all Composio users, while a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You need faster polling triggers.** Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You need custom scopes.** Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Managed apps use Composio's default scopes, which may not include everything a developer needs, such as write access to a specific Google API; custom scopes require the developer's own app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **Default scopes cover your needs.** Composio requests sensible defaults for each toolkit.
evidence.answer: Composio requests sensible default scopes for each toolkit when using managed apps.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You're connecting to a custom instance.** Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app rather than a managed one.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit, the page directs readers to the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You can still create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances.
evidence.answer: A developer can create a custom auth config for branding, scopes, rate limits, polling intervals, or custom instances even when a managed app exists.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You don't have to pick one approach for all toolkits. Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: Approach can be chosen per toolkit: a developer may use their own credentials for some toolkits and Composio managed auth for others, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

evidence.quote: To create an OAuth Application, sign in to your account , go to "Account Settings", scroll down and navigate to "Developer Settings" section. From the Developer Settings page, click "New Application" under the OAuth Applications section.
evidence.answer: OAuth apps are created in the web app: sign in, go to Account Settings, then Developer Settings, then click New Application under OAuth Applications.

evidence.answer: The current API version is v1.

evidence.answer: The API moved from youneedabudget.com to api.ynab.com in 2023; the old address still works but consumers should switch.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Display the privacy policy URL in your OAuth client configuration when your application is publicly available and ensure that it is prominently displayed in your application interface
evidence.answer: When the app is publicly available, its privacy policy URL must be shown in the OAuth client configuration and prominently in the app.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: a scope parameter with a value of read-only can be passed to request read-only access to a plan.
evidence.answer: The only scope value the page documents is read-only, which requests read-only access to a plan.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If an access token issued with the read-only scope is used when requesting an endpoint that modifies the plan (POST, PATCH, etc.) a 403 Forbidden response will be issued.
evidence.answer: A read-only token used on an endpoint that modifies the plan receives a 403 Forbidden response.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Only request the minimum necessary permissions to run your application, features, or services
evidence.answer: Apps should request only the minimum permissions needed to run.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Request access in context, via incremental authorization, wherever possible.
evidence.answer: Access should be requested in context, using incremental authorization wherever possible.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner
evidence.answer: Unreviewed apps in Restricted Mode are capped at 25 access tokens for users other than the owner.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: An access token may be used for up to 200 requests per hour
evidence.answer: Access tokens have a general limit of 200 requests per hour, on a rolling window.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: YNAB sets and enforces limits on your use of the APIs at our discretion.
evidence.answer: YNAB sets and enforces API usage limits at its own discretion, and they may change.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type does not support refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the user must be prompted again to authorize your application.
evidence.answer: Implicit grant tokens expire 2 hours after being granted, with no refresh token, so the user must re-authorize.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This grant type supports refresh tokens so once the access token expires 2 hours after it was granted, the application can request a new access token without having to prompt the user to authorize again.
evidence.answer: Authorization code grant tokens also expire 2 hours after being granted, but can be refreshed without re-authorization.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: This process takes 2-4 weeks.
evidence.answer: The review to remove Restricted Mode takes 2-4 weeks.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The subscription for this account has lapsed
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 subscription_lapsed error when the account's subscription has lapsed.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: The trial for this account has expired
evidence.answer: API requests return a 403 trial_expired error when the account's trial has expired.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may only be used when permission is explicitly given by a YNAB account owner through the Authentication processes described in the documentation above.
evidence.answer: API use requires explicit permission from a YNAB account owner, given through the documented authentication processes.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The user will be given the option to approve your request for access
evidence.answer: The end user is given the option to approve the app's access request.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: When default plan selection is enabled, a user will be asked to select a default plan when authorizing your application
evidence.answer: If default plan selection is enabled, the user chooses a default plan while authorizing the app.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: replacing [CLIENT_ID] and [REDIRECT_URI] with the values configured when creating the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI is set when the OAuth application is created.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The same [REDIRECT_URI] sent with the original authorization code request in Step 1 above and specified when setting up the OAuth Application.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI sent in the token request must match the one used in the authorization request and set at app setup.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: the user's browser will be redirected to the [REDIRECT_URI] with a new authorization code sent as a query parameter named code
evidence.answer: After approval, the browser is redirected to the redirect URI with the authorization code as a query parameter.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: a new access token sent as a fragment (hash) identifier named access_token
evidence.answer: In the implicit flow, the access token is sent to the redirect URI as a fragment (hash) identifier.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: TLS (a.k.a. SSL or HTTPS) is enforced on all requests to ensure communication from your client to our endpoint is encrypted,
evidence.answer: YNAB API requests must use HTTPS (TLS), which is enforced on all requests.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: After saving, you will see the details of the new application, including the Client ID and the Client Secret which are referenced in the instructions below.
evidence.answer: On saving the new application, its Client ID and Client Secret are displayed.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Here, you specify the details of your application and save it.
evidence.answer: Application details are entered on the New Application form and then saved.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The YNAB API supports two OAuth grant types: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant
evidence.answer: Two OAuth grant types are supported: Implicit Grant and Authorization Code Grant.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Send user to the authorization URL: https://app.ynab.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=[CLIENT_ID]&redirect_uri=[REDIRECT_URI]&response_type=code
evidence.answer: The authorization code flow sends users to app.ynab.com/oauth/authorize with the client ID, redirect URI and response type.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: https://app.ynab.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=[CLIENT_ID]&redirect_uri=[REDIRECT_URI]&response_type=token&scope=read-only
evidence.answer: Scope is set by adding a scope parameter to the authorization URL, for example scope=read-only.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: sending a POST request to https://app.ynab.com/oauth/token with the following parameters in the request body
evidence.answer: The authorization code is exchanged by POSTing to app.ynab.com/oauth/token with client ID, client secret, redirect URI, grant type and code.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The application Secret should never be visible or accessible by a client!
evidence.answer: The client secret must never be visible or accessible to a client.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: An OAuth application can optionally have 'default plan selection' enabled.
evidence.answer: Default plan selection is an optional setting for OAuth apps.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: limited to obtaining 25 access tokens for users other than the OAuth application owner
evidence.answer: Apps are restricted to 25 access tokens for other users while in Restricted Mode.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You may not use the YNAB API to copy or duplicate products or services offered by YNAB.
evidence.answer: Apps may not use the API to copy or duplicate YNAB's own products or services.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: you acknowledge that YNAB may, now or in the future, offer products, services, or features that are similar to your application.
evidence.answer: YNAB may offer products or features similar to the app now or in the future.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application and the web address (DNS name) must not include "YNAB" or "You Need A Budget" unless preceded by the word "for".
evidence.answer: The app name and web address (DNS name) may not include YNAB or You Need A Budget unless preceded by the word for.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Any graphics or artwork may not be modifications to our official branding
evidence.answer: Graphics or artwork must not modify YNAB's official branding and must be distinguishable from YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: To identify that your app integrates with YNAB, you may use this linked image and refer to
evidence.answer: Apps may use YNAB's linked image and refer to for YNAB in the app name to show integration.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: We are not affiliated, associated, or in any way officially connected with YNAB or any of its subsidiaries or affiliates.
evidence.answer: Apps must add a non-affiliation disclaimer at the footer of their site.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: you must be of a legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB
evidence.answer: Users must be of legal age to form a binding contract with YNAB.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Your application may not be directed or for children under 13.
evidence.answer: Apps may not be directed at or for children under 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The minimum age for a user to use YNAB is 13.
evidence.answer: The minimum age for a user to use YNAB is 13.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The application must not directly request, handle or store any financial account credentials other than an access token obtained directly from a financial institution using OAuth.
evidence.answer: Apps may not handle financial account credentials other than an OAuth access token obtained from a financial institution.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: The YNAB API may not be used for illegal purposes
evidence.answer: The YNAB API may not be used for illegal purposes.
